name: Tamegroute
hero_subtitle: Green pottery workshops and a historic Koranic library about 20 km south of Zagora.

overview.title: Clay, green glaze and manuscripts
overview.p1: Tamegroute is a small Draa village known across Morocco for its green-glazed pottery and for the zaouia’s historic library of manuscripts.
overview.p2: You can watch potters at work, browse ceramics, and — when access allows — see the library’s collection of religious and scientific texts. It is a culture stop rather than a sand or dune day.
overview.p3: Go with respect for religious spaces, ask before photographing people at work, and leave time for the road back to Zagora.

q1.question: How far from Zagora?
q1.answer: About 20 km south on the main road.

q2.question: Can I buy pottery?
q2.answer: Yes — workshops and stalls sell the distinctive green pieces.

q3.question: Library access?
q3.answer: Often possible; a small donation may be expected — confirm on arrival.

q4.question: Combine with Tinfou?
q4.answer: Yes — dunes and Tamegroute sit in the same southern outing for many visitors.

q5.question: How long?
q5.answer: One and a half to three hours covers pottery and library without rushing.
